summary: Replaced the bundled release action's single timed upload flow with an idempotent publisher using GitVerse's documented release and multipart-asset endpoints. Six local tests cover creation, multipart payload, lost-response recovery, retry, repeated jobs, conflicting assets and missing credentials. The Windows runner and a real tagged release have not yet been exercised.

checks.name: Publisher contract and retry tests
checks.observation: All six tests pass using a mocked GitVerse API. Tests verify multipart attachment, a bounded 15-minute request timeout, transient retry, reconciling an accepted upload after a lost response, skipping an already-present same-size asset, rejecting conflicting assets and failing closed without RELEASE_API_KEY.

checks.name: JavaScript syntax, workflow YAML and diff checks
checks.command: node --check scripts/android_release/publish.mjs && node --check scripts/android_release/publish.test.mjs; Ruby YAML parse for both Android Release and Flutter Windows CI workflows; git diff --check
checks.observation: Both workflow files parse as YAML, JavaScript syntax checks pass and the diff has no whitespace errors.

checks.name: GitVerse Windows runner test
checks.observation: The release-publisher suite was added to the Flutter Windows workflow but no run for this change has completed yet.
